audit.note: Scoped re-audit of the cycle-1 repair (3 sentences changed, form unchanged; not expanded, since the argument, assumptions, structure and scope are unchanged). The removed paragraph 6 sentence is replaced by one that refers back to paragraph 1's length check instead of restating it, so the point is no longer made twice. Re-read every changed sentence, its paragraph, and every other use of 'unambiguous', 'number of elements', 'position' and 'length': consistent. Accuracy of the new claims checked: with the count known and uniform leaf depth, a presented internal node's proof is shorter than every valid proof and is rejected; RFC 6962 prefixes, Bitcoin's shared double SHA-256 and 64-byte transactions, the mutated-tree check, and OpenZeppelin's sorted-pair hashing are correctly stated. Parent overlap: State Commitments (only placement) says nothing about Merkle trees; no restatement. Territory: hash-functions and merkle-patricia-tries named only; no sibling's label (state-proofs absence, state-roots, verkle) explained; all four labels still explained. Representation: the recomputation comparison is unchanged and accurate per row. Canonical validity: no positional or time-sensitive words, American English, plain text. Depth: the repair added about a dozen words; each paragraph still serves a label. Advisory: (1) 'one level shorter' / 'one level short' holds only for an internal node directly above the leaves; a node h levels up yields a proof h levels short, so 'shorter' would be exact. (2) The paragraph 6 length-check sentence covers only the presented-node half of the first case; the same-root different-collection half is removed by separation (or a committed count), which the paragraph could make explicit.

Re-read the whole paragraph, the comparison and every other use of branch/extension/leaf and 'part' (proof paragraph, absence cases, insertion split, deletion collapse): no contradiction introduced, no new term or sense, no widened scope. Overlap per placement (one placement, State Commitments parent): the changed sentence restates nothing in the parent or the domain line. Territory: the sentence stays within 'which node types shorten that path'; no sibling or excluded concept is explained. Representation: the comparison remains the right structure; the summary sentence draws the consequence for a whole path, which the per-node rows do not state outright, so it is not a spelled-out copy of the table. audit.note: Re-audit of state-roots after repair, scoped by l2 repair-diff (5 sentences removed, 6 added, form unchanged; paragraphs 3 and 6 changed). Not expanded into a full audit: the repair fixed statements at their scope and changed neither the argument, its assumptions, the structure nor the scope; the whole record was nevertheless read. Resolved: paragraph 3 no longer says the producer of every block records the root of its own execution and that validators reject the block on mismatch, which contradicted paragraph 4's CometBFT case; it now conditions the same-block check on headers that record their own execution's root (Ethereum) and states that on CometBFT chains the result is recorded in, and checked against, the next block's header (CometBFT validation rejects a block whose app hash differs from the state the node computed), and the divergence sentence now says nodes part ways 'at the first recorded root that exposes the difference', which holds under both recording rules. Paragraph 6 no longer claims the state root is the one header commitment that accumulates (the parent hash also reaches back through history); it is scoped to headers such as Ethereum's, says the effects of execution accumulate in the state root, and distinguishes the parent hash as linking earlier headers without fixing the state this block leaves, consistent with the comparison's parent-hash row. Checked every use of the changed terms (recorded root, producer, next block's header, accumulate, parent hash) across paragraphs 3, 4, 6, the comparison and paragraph 7: consistent. Overlap per placement: nothing restates the State Commitments, State Representation or Cross-Chain State parent texts; the Cross-Chain State parent's sentence on header relaying is not restated. Territory: changes stay within 'how a state root is recomputed ... and where a protocol records it' and 'how a state root differs from the other commitments a block records'; excluded concepts remain named only. Representation unchanged and still accurate. American English, plain text, no positional words. Advisory: (1) the repair made paragraph 3 repeat paragraph 4's point that Ethereum headers record their own block's post-state root while CometBFT headers record the previous block's, with the same 'executed only after it has been agreed on' reason; one of the two statements could be reduced to a reference, which would also bring the record back under the depth-long threshold; (2) 'the root of that block's own execution' would read more precisely as 'the root of the state after that block's own execution', the wording paragraph 4 uses.

groupAudit.note: Group audit of state-commitments: the five owned members (merkle-trees, merkle-patricia-tries, verkle-trees, state-roots, state-proofs) read side by side against the plan, the reserved commitment-schemes labels and the parent State Commitments. Territory: no member explains what another's labels cover. Absence is divided by angle (merkle-trees: positions, sorting, sparse default leaves; merkle-patricia-tries: where a key's path leaves the trie; verkle-trees: empty slot or another key's stem; state-proofs: which statements a proof can establish, deferring to the structure). Root trust is owned by state-roots (three facts); merkle-trees and state-proofs only state in one boundary sentence each that a proof does not authenticate the root and name state roots. The two-trie storage proof is explained in merkle-patricia-tries and only referenced in state-proofs (cost) and state-roots (account fields). Reserved commitment-schemes labels are not crossed: verkle-trees names binding, homomorphic update and opening size per scheme only as its width and assumption labels need; state-roots and state-proofs name the commitment scheme only. No split exists. Contradictions: none found. Checked: wide nodes enlarge proofs in a tree of hashes (merkle-trees) agrees with the three-to-four-times figure for sixteen-way branch nodes (merkle-patricia-tries) and with verkle-trees' contrast that openings omit siblings; forging a hash-tree proof needs a collision given an unambiguous construction (merkle-trees, verkle-trees, state-roots) is stated with the same condition each time; the MPT root depending only on current keys (merkle-patricia-tries) agrees with state-roots' history-independence example, and IAVL's order dependence is correctly kept separate; sparse-tree absence as a default value (merkle-trees) agrees with state-proofs' absence-equals-default statement for Ethereum storage. Terms: binding, opening, unambiguous construction, tree of hashes and inclusion/absence are used in one sense across members. Representation: four members carry one comparison and state-proofs a distinction; each comparison has different alternatives and dimensions decided by its own claim (recomputation by kind of change, node kinds as a lookup meets them, forging assumptions by commitment, an Ethereum header's four commitments), so this is not one cloned form, and the group signal for one form did not fire. Convergence: the five definitional openings ('A ... is ...') follow the definition-leads rule, not imitation; the shared arc of the three structure records (path, proof contents, proof size, update cost) follows their parallel labels, and verkle-trees and merkle-patricia-tries diverge after it (assumptions; storage and pruning). Drift window shows no convergence flag. Group signals: none to resolve. Advisory: (1) state-roots states twice that CometBFT records the result in the next block's header and that Ethereum records its own block's root (paragraph 4 and paragraph 5); one could refer back to the other. (2) The shared-upper-levels saving of combined proofs is made in merkle-trees (size) and again in state-proofs (cost); state-proofs could shorten its clause to a reference.
